probe_notes: Second run. Only 4 days since seed (2026-04-30), so no score movement is expected — vendor pipelines don't ship weekly. Two notable documentation signals: (1) Adam now lists a Fusion 360 Extension alongside the Onshape Extension on its homepage — second-platform unlock since seed, still extension-locked on both substrates; (2) Zoo.dev confirms GD&T/MBD annotation endpoints (flatness, datum) and ML reasoning WebSocket, deepening engineering signal without yet reaching structured process-level DfM. Shapr3D announced Apple Vision Pro support — no API surface added. Spline Code API for Web/SwiftUI/Kotlin is for scene-embedding in apps, not agent-to-agent calls. Fusion AI APS page returned JavaScript bootstrap — no new AI API surface found. First real deltas expected in week 3+ as vendors respond to market pressure.

parametric_edit.notes: Add/Delete Feature endpoints confirmed in API docs. KCL (Kit-CAD Language) is purpose-built parametric scripting that an agent can write to edit assemblies end-to-end. Multi-file CAD iteration endpoint confirmed (/ml/text-to-cad/multi-file/iteration).

feature_tree_introspection.notes: Mass, volume, surface-area, density, bounding-box, and center-of-mass endpoints documented. Zoo MCP supports 'inspecting design files and parametric code (KCL).' Full model-state read access confirmed.

structured_output.notes: REST APIs use JSON request/response bodies with OpenAPI spec at root endpoint for schema-driven client generation. Strict, parseable, predictable. KCL completions endpoint also schema-driven.

mcp_compat.notes: Public MCP server (zoo-mcp) documented — 'a bridge between an AI client and Zoo's design tools.' Setup: `uvx zoo-mcp` with ZOO_API_TOKEN. Explicitly supports Claude, Codex, and other MCP-compatible clients. First CAD vendor with a published MCP.

headless_mode.notes: TypeScript, Python, Rust, Go SDKs plus CLI (`zoo kcl`, `zoo file`, `zoo ml` subcommands) plus direct HTTP. API-first design = pure headless capable with no display dependency.

auth_accessibility.notes: Bearer-token auth via API tokens created from user accounts (self-serve). OAuth2 device authorization grant and provider-based consent flows also documented. Service account support for org-level automation.

diff_friendly_export.notes: KCL is a parametric scripting language stored as text — line-level git-diffable. `zoo kcl format` and `zoo kcl lint` commands promote consistency. Code-as-CAD by design.

dfm_feedback.notes: GD&T/MBD annotation support confirmed this run (flatness, datum annotations in Design Studio). No wall-thickness, process-level DfM, or manufacturing constraint endpoints found in API docs. GD&T is tolerancing specification, not process-level manufacturability feedback — score holds at 5. v2 candidate to upgrade if structured DfM endpoints ship.

notable_changes: GD&T/MBD annotation support (flatness, datum) confirmed in Design Studio — tolerancing signal deepens but no dedicated DfM API endpoint found
ML reasoning WebSocket (/ws/ml/reasoning/{id}) and multi-file CAD iteration endpoint confirmed — ML inference layer maturing

parametric_edit.notes: POST + DELETE HTTP methods documented. FeatureScript API supports programmatic feature creation and edit. Features API guide documented at /docs/api-adv/featureaccess/. Multi-feature chain editing within parts well-supported; full assembly editing via REST is partial.

feature_tree_introspection.notes: Full GET endpoints for documents, parts, assemblies, features. Schema-defined, versioned (v6). Real-time access to the Onshape engine and data. JSON responses with documented field schemas.

structured_output.notes: RESTful with JSON bodies, well-defined schemas, versioned endpoints. X-Deprecated and X-Rate-Limit headers documented. Enterprise-grade structured output.

mcp_compat.notes: REST + OAuth + community SDKs (Python, JS) — fully callable by an external agent over HTTP. No first-party MCP server published yet (community work emerging). Scores 10 (REST/HTTP callable) not 15 (no MCP or formal tool definitions).

headless_mode.notes: Pure REST API — runs anywhere with HTTP + auth. Documented production use in CI / build pipelines. No display dependency.

auth_accessibility.notes: OAuth (/docs/auth/oauth/) and API keys (/docs/auth/apikeys/) both documented as primary auth flows. Self-serve key generation for individual / dev accounts.

diff_friendly_export.notes: FeatureScript is plain text and diffs cleanly. Native Onshape document format is binary; STEP/STL exports are binary. Mixed: text-diffable for FeatureScript code, opaque for geometry blobs.

dfm_feedback.notes: No DfM endpoints found in REST API docs. DfM is in-product (visual warnings in the UI), not exposed programmatically.

parametric_edit.notes: Community LLM-to-SCAD tools generate or modify SCAD code. Parametric Customizer documented in user manual. Scope mostly single-feature or small script edits; full assembly scope depends on script structure and LLM context. No defining first-party tool.

feature_tree_introspection.notes: OpenSCAD has no traditional feature tree — script-based system. LLM tools can read the SCAD script as text but cannot introspect a parametric tree per se. Scoring 5 (names-only equivalent: variable names + module structure visible in plain text).

structured_output.notes: LLM-driven tools output SCAD code — structured text, parseable but not schema-compliant. No formal change-log format across community tools.

mcp_compat.notes: Community MCP wrappers and CLI tooling exist around OpenSCAD; nothing first-party. No formal cross-agent contract. Scores 5 (browser-extension-equivalent: community orbit, no stable API contract).

headless_mode.notes: Documented 'Using OpenSCAD in a command line environment' — `openscad -o output.stl input.scad` is canonical. WebAssembly node.js standalone build also documented. Maximum headless capability.

auth_accessibility.notes: Free, open-source, no authentication required. An agent can pull the binary and run it without any onboarding friction. Maximum accessibility.

diff_friendly_export.notes: SCAD files are plain text. Perfect git-diff. Code-as-CAD in its original form — the benchmark all other vendors are measured against.

dfm_feedback.notes: OpenSCAD has no built-in DfM signal. Some community libraries add manufacturability hints, but nothing standardized or machine-readable.

parametric_edit.notes: Positions as 'First AI CAD Copilot for Mechanical CAD Software'. Capabilities include text-to-3D generating STEP/STL, plus task automation across sketching, constraints, drawings, bulk exports on SolidWorks and Inventor. Multi-feature chain scope confirmed; full-assembly scope not explicitly documented.

feature_tree_introspection.notes: Constraint and sketch automation requires reading existing feature tree state. Real-time pricing capability implies model-context awareness across the full part/assembly.

structured_output.notes: UI-driven actions in SolidWorks/Inventor. No documented diff format, change-log, or structured output surface found. No API docs published.

mcp_compat.notes: Desktop plugin lock-in (SolidWorks + Inventor live; CATIA, Fusion 360, NX, SolidEdge, Onshape, Creo planned). Same scoring shape as Adam: works inside host app UI, no headless / programmatic call path documented.

headless_mode.notes: Desktop CAD application required. No CLI / SDK / headless build documented.

auth_accessibility.notes: Self-serve download via download.mecagent.com/dashboard/plan; demo-booking option for enterprise. Falls into self-serve sign-up tier.

diff_friendly_export.notes: Native binary formats (SLDPRT, IPT). Documented exports are PDF/DXF/DRW — also non-parametric, not git-diffable.

dfm_feedback.notes: Standards compliance checks documented as a core capability — partial DfM-adjacent signal (compliance-flavored rather than purely manufacturability-flavored). Not yet structured machine-readable output. v2 candidate to upgrade once output format is documented.

parametric_edit.notes: Feature Tree Optimization (find/merge duplicate features), Parametrization (cascade variables throughout design), and Selection Context (high-level command using selected CAD context) — chain-of-features within one part confirmed. Full assembly scope not documented. Now runs on both Onshape and Fusion 360 substrates.

feature_tree_introspection.notes: Selection Context takes a high-level command and uses the selected CAD context to create new features — requires reading current model state. Tree + dimensions implied by parametric edit scope.

structured_output.notes: Output format not documented. No published schema for the diff Adam applies to CAD models. v2 candidate to probe via direct extension inspection.

mcp_compat.notes: Browser extension on Onshape + Fusion 360 extension (new this run). YC profile confirms 'Co-Pilot that integrates within professional CAD workflows' — still extension-shaped on both substrates. No public REST or MCP path documented. Score holds at 5 (extension lock-in, two hosts).

headless_mode.notes: Chrome extension + Fusion plugin required. No CLI, no headless build documented on either substrate.

auth_accessibility.notes: 'Try Adam Web App' + 'Install Adam Extension' suggest self-serve sign-up. No documented API key flow yet.

diff_friendly_export.notes: Outputs CAD host internal format (Onshape binary, Fusion .f3d). STL export is also binary. No parametric-script export documented.

dfm_feedback.notes: No DfM signal surfaced in public materials. Some basic warnings possible in demos; no structured output. v2 candidate for deeper probe.

notable_changes: Fusion 360 Extension now listed on adam.new homepage alongside Onshape Extension — second-platform unlock since seed run (Apr 30). mcp_compat stays 5: extension lock-in persists on both substrates.

parametric_edit.notes: Autodesk Platform Services (APS) offers some Fusion API surface, but AI features (generative design, AI assistant) are largely in-app and not programmatically callable. Single-feature edit at best via public APS surface.

feature_tree_introspection.notes: Partial introspection via APS Data Management + Model Derivative APIs. Names-level access; deep parametric tree access is in-product only.

structured_output.notes: AI features not documented in public APS API surface. No structured output schema for the AI assistant. APS page loaded as JavaScript bootstrap this run — no new AI API surface found.

mcp_compat.notes: AI features are in-app only. APS is a different surface (file management + viewing); no MCP, no agent-callable AI endpoint documented.

headless_mode.notes: Fusion 360 is a desktop application. AI features require the running desktop instance.

auth_accessibility.notes: APS access for many production use cases requires business verification / sales engagement. Not self-serve in the same way Onshape REST is.

diff_friendly_export.notes: Native .f3d format is binary. STEP/STL export downstream also binary.

dfm_feedback.notes: Generative design has manufacturability constraints baked in (manufacturing methods as inputs). Not exposed as a structured DfM API; warnings live in the desktop UI.

parametric_edit.notes: Spline AI features (Spell, AI 3D Generation, AI Textures, AI Style Transfer) operate on web-3D scenes. Single-element edits implied; web/product-design audience, not mechanical CAD. 'Working with Parametric Objects' documented but not detailed.

feature_tree_introspection.notes: Not documented for the AI features in this run.

structured_output.notes: Real-time API and Webhooks listed under Variables & Data but response schemas not documented in available content.

mcp_compat.notes: Code API for Web/SwiftUI/Kotlin is for embedding Spline scenes in apps (runtime viewer SDK), not for agent-to-agent CAD edit calls. No MCP or external edit API documented.

headless_mode.notes: Browser app. AI features run in-product. Code API is client-side embedding only.

auth_accessibility.notes: Self-serve sign-up for the editor. No documented API key flow for AI features.

diff_friendly_export.notes: Spline scene format is opaque. GLTF/GLB, USDZ, STL exports are binary.

dfm_feedback.notes: Web 3D — DfM-irrelevant. Probe row included for category completeness; candidate for v2 hide if it dilutes leaderboard signal.

parametric_edit.notes: AI features mentioned ('AI + Live AR design reviews', 'AI renders'). Single-feature edit at best from what's surfaced. Apple Vision Pro support announced this run — immersive design reviews, no programmatic surface added.

feature_tree_introspection.notes: No public API or plugin SDK documented. Developer inquiries routed to contact-sales.

mcp_compat.notes: GUI-only (Windows / macOS / iPad / Vision Pro). No API, no plugin SDK, no documented programmatic access.

headless_mode.notes: Multi-platform GUI app. All operations in-product.

diff_friendly_export.notes: Exports: 3MF, STL, STEP, XT, IGES, OBJ confirmed this run — all binary formats. Native format binary. No parametric script export.

notable_changes: Apple Vision Pro support announced — immersive XR design reviews added as a platform; no API surface or programmatic access added alongside.

headlines: Zoo.dev holds top composite at 90/100 for week 2 — GD&T/MBD annotations and ML reasoning WebSocket confirmed, but no structured process-level DfM endpoint ships yet; dfm_feedback stays at 5.
Adam expands to Fusion 360 — plugin now multi-platform (Onshape + Fusion), first capability delta since seed; score holds at 30 as extension lock-in persists on both substrates and no API path added.
No score movement across 8 vendors week-over-week — probe cadence shorter than vendor ship cycle; first real deltas expected week 3+ as the ZooMCP ecosystem and Adam Co-Pilot roadmap mature.
